purpose: Preregister precision-specific correctness checks before BF16 execution; do not relax thresholds after observing results.
comparison: For every vocabulary logit at every generated step, both sides must be finite and abs(candidate-reference) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference); all greedy token IDs must match.

float32.note: Retain every existing FP32 acceptance comparison and additionally validate the tokenwise HF control.

bfloat16.primary_reference: HF prefix prefill in one batch, then one HF forward per suffix token, then one token per decode step, matching custom operator input shapes.
bfloat16.note: Full recompute and batched suffix references are retained as chunking diagnostics. Their BF16 numerical differences alone do not determine migration correctness. Failure of the primary strict comparison is reported as failure without automatic tolerance relaxation.

common_requirements: Requested dtype must match every floating model parameter, immutable prefix tensor, and Q/K/V or attention-output tensor crossing the wire.
Peer identity includes dtype, numerical backend settings, protocol hash, model manifest hash, and source hashes.
TF32 is disabled and float32 matmul precision is highest; BF16 and FP16 reduction settings are recorded.
Each of the three HF controls owns a fresh cache and reports final length prefix + suffix + generated - 1.
Control GPU caches are released before the next reference or custom run; only CPU comparison logits and token IDs are retained.
logits_to_keep=1 is enabled only when model.forward explicitly declares that parameter; its output sequence length is checked and forward signature/source hash are recorded.
The immutable holder prefix is ready before the request barrier; the hit path never prefills the prefix.
Existing delta-length, cross-node identity, and progressive repair acceptance checks remain required.
limitations: Correctness development only; this protocol does not establish serving performance or paper-scale results.
BF16 acceptance establishes equivalence to the tokenwise HF reference, not chunk-invariance across different HF batching strategies.
Native BF16 still requires actual GPU validation; static checks are not execution evidence.
